answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a dawn as the anchor of the cost.
